source_audit: R1800 preserves original measurable-level overlap through an explicit regularization budget, then composes with the actual smoothed autocorrelation nonflattening theorem. This is supporting formalization, not a new impossibility theorem. Bourgain–Yehudayoff, Monotone expansion, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1108.2555, Section4.1, equations4.11–4.12 and Theorem4.4 rechecked R1800: after approximate-group concentration, the source obtains local small-ball overlap and a scale-sensitive covering bound before invoking product growth. The source product theorem requires intermediate size, multiscale distribution and quantitative escape; finite covering alone does not prove flattening. Our conservative explicit constants and actual autocorrelation densities remain in force.

The regularization error is chosen after the level's loss parameter, with an exact half-budget absorption. Composition with actual smoothed autocorrelation nonflattening gives U, finite symmetric Y subset U^2 and x, all with explicit entry bounds, volume bounds and a positive probability bound for x*U under H.withDensity(rho_k). The logarithmic dyadic-level count is retained. No small-ball thickness or scale-sensitive cover is assumed. The original-density concentration target is complete; smoothing-scale local overlap and finite covering, product growth/escape, strict flattening and unconditional paid padding remain unproved. These are supporting formalizations of known arguments, not new transposition bounds.
